## Close evidence — caller analysis (AC3), recorded by the orchestrator

The implementing agent landed the change but did not write evidence back to this ticket, so AC3
("the split follows a pre-existing call-graph seam, WITH THE CALLER ANALYSIS RECORDED") was
literally unmet. Performing and recording that analysis here, verified against merged main.

### The split
Gerrit change 1426, MERGED as dc26a34e399, LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.
`passes.py` 800 -> 595 (AC1: under 700, met). New sibling
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/completion_subcall.py` at 288 lines (AC2: >= 100, met).
The diff touches ONLY those two files -- zero test edits (AC4 met).

### The extracted cluster
Two module constants plus `_pass2_completion_model`, `_delivered_manifest_block`,
`_completion_finding_listing`, `_coerce_completion_enum`, `_coerce_attribution`,
`pass2_completion`, and `completion_floor_drop`. One concern: the pass-2 completion sub-call and
the pass-3 completion floor, with their private helpers.

### Caller analysis — is it a PRE-EXISTING seam?
Reference counts, in-module versus everywhere else in src/ and tests/:

    _delivered_manifest_block    in-module 3   outside 0
    _coerce_completion_enum      in-module 4   outside 0
    _coerce_attribution          in-module 3   outside 0
    _pass2_completion_model      in-module 3   outside 3  (all the re-export path)
    _completion_finding_listing  in-module 3   outside 3

Three helpers have ZERO references outside the extracted module, so they moved with their only
caller -- the definition of an existing seam rather than a mechanical cut.

### The module-attribute hazard was handled correctly
`_completion_finding_listing` is the exception, and it is the important one:
`tests/unit/test_plan_review_completion.py:165` calls it as
`passes._completion_finding_listing(findings)` -- a MODULE-ATTRIBUTE access, not an import. The
re-export at `passes.py:92` (with `# noqa: F401`) preserves that access, and `passes.py:85`
documents why in-line.

This is exactly the hazard that task c6c9 proved is real rather than theoretical when it applied
the naive-import mutation and four tests went RED. Worth recording that it recurred here one
ticket later, and was handled.

### AC5 (operator-attested: full suite passes with equal test count)
I did NOT run a local full-suite count, so I am not attesting a count. The evidence is CI: the
full suite passed on four clean checkouts (ubuntu py3.11/3.12/3.13 + macos py3.13) yielding
Verified +1 on the merged patchset. That is stronger evidence than a local count on this host,
where the worktree venvs run Python 3.14.6 -- outside the tested matrix (bug a5f5-1059-cc11-4af6).

### Follow-on
`passes.py` is no longer the largest file in the package, but the module-size problem is
repo-wide: 40 files over 700 LOC, three within two lines of the hard cap. Tracked as story
5e53-234f-5c65-477d rather than as further one-file tickets.
